summary.headline: Jagsonpal Q4 FY26 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR64 crores and PAT 31% to ~INR9 crores; MAT growth 12.2% vs IPM ~7-8%.
summary.overview: Management says Jagsonpal returned to growth in Q4 after two sluggish quarters, with Pharmarack data showing 14.2% Q4 growth against 10.5% for the industry. FY26 revenue grew about 7% to INR287 crores, while profit from operations grew 19% to about INR45 crores before the one-time labour code charge taken in Q3. The board announced a INR40 crore buyback at INR250 per share (no promoter participation) and a 200% dividend including a 75% special, together returning over INR66 crores. Management reiterated a target of 1.5x IPM growth, which it translates to 12-15% currently.

segments.name: Gynaecology
segments.commentary: Roughly half of business per management; named as the largest growth driver with Dermatology, with prescription momentum and improved doctor conversion.

segments.name: Orthopaedics
segments.commentary: Roughly 25% of business; overweight therapy, but management said in Q&A it is in line with IPM currently. A dedicated Ortho franchise is still being built.

segments.name: Dermatology
segments.commentary: Roughly 10-15% of business; second growth driver after Gynaecology. Ranked third on MR productivity.

guidance_outlook: Target growth of 1.5x IPM; management translated current IPM of 6-9% into 12-15% company growth and said it maintains this guidance for FY27.
Planned 9-10 product launches in FY27, of which about half are legacy brand extensions and 5-6 are new products in existing strength therapies.
Expects growth to get better over the next two quarters on Pharmarack-reflected numbers.
Buyback of INR40 crores at INR250/share (up to 16 lakh shares) approved by shareholders on 27 April; record date 4 May 2026. Expected to lift ROE from ~16% to ~18% and ROCE from ~22% to ~26%.
Dividend of 200% (INR4/share incl. 75% special), total cash outgo ~INR26 crores, subject to AGM approval.
Management said it can raise over INR200 crores of fresh debt and has balance-sheet capacity for acquisitions up to ~INR400 crores; an acquisition announcement is not yet made.
capex_capacity: MR headcount unchanged; no new MRs added in the last quarter. Growth to come from productivity of existing field force and geographies.
Asset-light model using CMOs; management says cost pressure is mainly packaging material and insurance costs, passed on over time under longer-term CMO agreements.
Price increases are SKU-based and taken after 12 months; ~92% of portfolio is outside NLEM price control, allowing up to 9.9% increase per management.
Strategic initiatives on field-force retention, internal promotions and MR upskilling are in progress.
demand_pricing: Pharmarack MAT (FY26) Jagsonpal growth 12.2% vs IPM ~8.5-9% (volume ~1-2%, new products ~3%, price ~5-7%); Q4 Jagsonpal 14.2% vs industry 10.5%. Management noted reported Pharmarack figure is 7% vs 12% on its mirrored basis, attributed to lead-lag.
Top 10 brands ~58-60% of sales; nine of them rank in top five in their categories. Growth of top 10 brands said to be in line with the rest of portfolio.
Management says the Middle East situation has no demand impact; cost pressure is on packaging materials, with vendors passing on increases.
Management said e-pharmacy channel is almost insignificant for revenue. A mature brand moderation in some therapies was offset by Gynae and Derma.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 recovery structural or seasonal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the portfolio has hardly any seasonal products and the growth is driven by operational strengthening, brand building and MR productivity.

qa_highlights.question: Why distribute so much cash rather than deploy it in the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Board says the pharma business is brand-intensive, not capital-intensive; surplus cash is for inorganic growth only, and it could raise over INR200 crores of debt for acquisitions of up to INR400 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin and other expense trends in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year gross margin about 64.2%, down 20-30 bps from product mix; other expenses up ~30 bps from timing of annual cycle meeting, with structural cost increases only inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 1.5x IPM target stand after the outperformance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained the 1.5x IPM target, which it says means 12-15% now, and said it expects the market to improve as metabolic and anti-obesity launches come through.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of growth into price, volume and new products?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 industry: volume ~1%, new products ~3.1%, price ~4.8%. Jagsonpal: volume ~2%, new products ~3.2%, price 6-7%.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q4 numbers a one-off and how is the portfolio diversifying?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says focus stays on 2-3 power brands per vertical, and new products are targeted at 3%+ contribution; new product establishment takes a year-plus to build prescriptions.

risks_watch: Sustainability of the outperformance: Q4 growth 14.2% vs industry 10.5%; management says the next two quarters should improve, which is a near-term test.
Cost pressure from packaging material and insurance costs passed on through CMO contracts; management says no significant profit impact.
Dependence on top 10 brands (58-60% of sales) and moderation in some mature brands.
Management said the new product launch announcement is expected by late May or early June 2026, which will show whether the pipeline holds.
Capital allocation: cash will fall after buyback and special dividend; management is open to an acquisition funded by debt of up to INR200 crores.
Trade generics and Jan Aushadhi competition; management says no validated data shows it eroding branded volumes.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Q4 turnaround and the 1.5x IPM target, but vague on segment-level detail: several answers deferred figures (therapy-wise growth, MR productivity by therapy, top 10 brand growth). Some responses were evasive on capital allocation.
key_quotes: Jagsonpal is back on growth in Q4 after two quarters of sluggish performance.
So any use of real cash that we have is only for inorganic strategy and not otherwise.
We continue to maintain that guidance, sir.
So technically we do have wherewithal to undertake an acquisition of up to INR400 crores with our own balance sheet.

growth.why: Management maintains a 1.5x IPM growth target, translated to 12-15% company growth for FY27, backed by 9-10 planned launches (5-6 new products), Pharmarack-tracked share gains (Q4 14.2% vs industry 10.5%) and ~9.9% price headroom, but no capacity additions are disclosed and MR headcount is flat.
